summary: Submitted draft/submission.json (action=check) with draft/check-plan-race.json and draft/check-harness-race.go: the second scenario of the accepted requirement c-client-request-completes-on-inactive-raft, and exactly the case its earlier review recorded as outside that check's prefix — a request the API accepts while the node is still leading and that a later shutdown leaves unresolved. No new obligation and no map change were needed, because the accepted claim's scope already covers the window in which a client call is raced with Shutdown; the check is attached to the existing unit and cites its selected binding, with the apply path cited by its own source ranges. The harness parks a single-voter leader inside its own dispatch path through a LogStore that holds exactly one StoreLogs call (a latency injection on an injected dependency), gives the node the documented BatchApplyCh option so applyCh is buffered, queues 200 further requests from goroutines so that the buffer fills and the rest block inside the API's enqueue select, and then shuts the node down; after the shutdown future has joined every raft goroutine it classifies each request by what the public API returned (a future for an accepted request, ErrRaftShutdown for a rejected one) and inspects the accepted futures' own completion channels without blocking. I verified the exact harness locally before it was moved into the draft: the test passes (exit 0) and reports, identically in three runs, requests_issued_while_active with the node reporting itself Leader and the main goroutine parked, then accepted_requests_observed with accepted 64, rejected_shutdown 136, unresolved_total 64 and the node in state Shutdown, so the assertion that accepted requests must all have completed is violated by sixty-four futures the node accepted while leading and never answered. The plan records the discriminator, the fixed inputs, the binding, the oracle (the accepted futures' own channels, with the rejected count kept separate so ErrRaftShutdown results are never counted as owed work), and its limits. Counterevidence and limits are explicit: the parked dispatch path is what makes the buffer fill deterministically, the exact counts depend on the buffer size and on how many requests the loop picks up before it takes the shutdown case, the default unbuffered channel cannot accept a request that shutdown later abandons (which is what the first scenario showed), only the Apply path with BatchApplyCh is exercised, and no caller-side timeout is measured so the practical blocking of a caller remains inferred. Optional preflight with the trusted validator returned valid=true; the next step would be the correspondence review of this second scenario, which is a new artifact under the same accepted claim.
